newsitem.title: USA: Agouron sees strong demand for Viracept.
newsitem.headline: Agouron sees strong demand for Viracept.

text.p: Agouron Pharmaceuticals Inc President Peter Johnson said he is confident the company's Viracept AIDS drug candidate could compete well with the three protease inhibitors now on the market. He said it could also carve out a part of the emerging two-drug AIDS therapy.

Speaking at the Hambrecht and Quist Healthcare conference here, Johnson said the company will report data later this month showing Viracept is highly potent, and provides a more flexible dosing schedule with fewer side effects than some of the protease inhibitors that have been approved to date.
"The data showed a brisk response and a remarkably low discontinuation rate," Johnson said. "We are now very busy with Phase 4 trials."

The company late last year filed a New Drug Application for Viracept with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. The three protease inhibitors that the FDA has so far approved, are made by Roche, Merck and Abbot Laboratories.
Because this class of drug is a cornerstone in the breakthrough three- drug therapy that has been shown to dramatically reduce viral load in a large share of AIDS patients, demand is strong.

However, Johnson said, protease inhibitors are still only used by about 100,000 of the estimated 850,000 AIDS patients in the U.S. "There can still be a tremendous amount of additional penetration," he said.
In addition, Johnson said he saw a potential market for Viracept in the emerging two-drug therapy, consisting of two protease inhibitors.
He said initial data on the combination of Abbott and Roche drugs was "encouraging."
"If the data holds, the two-drug therapy could stand to challenge the three-drug threatment," he said. "We could be well on our way to seeing a new paradigm for HIV treatment."
